summary: OptiIQ v8 (average of 9 methods) tested. Backend: 25/30 pass. stock-analysis long (MSFT 521.03, AAPL 241.80, TSLA 144.05, JPM 847.48) returns all 9 methods in the right order, count, the plain average, upside_pct and intrinsic_value rule, with no NaN or Infinity. The 17 unit tests pass. Board auth, shape, 5 buckets, d math and 404 for ZZZZ and ECHO all pass. CRITICAL: board 'v' does not match /valuation/board/{t} for most stocks. ANOTHER PROCESS outside this backend writes to the shared Atlas valuation_board collection with model_v=8 and a different formula. It overwrote values every price cycle while I watched: AAPL went 175.06 (other writer) -> 241.80 (ours, once our price_loop ran) -> 175.06 again. Frontend: MSFT card, 9 rows, values, note open and close, 'Average of 9 methods' footer, bar-only dashed lines, board buckets, search, chip, sheet, close, 'Full long-term analysis', LCID unavailable (avg below zero), CCI low-confidence warning, and the Discover, Chain, Portfolio, Alerts and Learn tabs all work. No red screens or page errors.

critical.issue: Two processes write db.valuation_board in the shared Atlas DB. The other one (likely the web app or an older deployed backend) uses model_v=8 with a different OptiIQ formula and keeps overwriting value/premium/bucket/price_ts. Evidence: (1) I saw AAPL flip 175.06 -> 241.80 -> 175.06 within minutes. (2) Unrated reasons include 'Not enough positive earnings or cash flow', which is not in current optiiq.py. (3) Docs still carry capex_history, a model 7 field. Result: board chip AAPL shows +96% while its sheet shows OptiIQ $241.80 (price about 42% above value). CCI sits in 'fair' (-5%) and BAC in a bucket with v 39.53, but current code says low-confidence, so both should be unrated. Sample mismatches: GDDY 317.88 vs 200.73, KMI 46.45 vs 102.25, TJX 172.92 vs 357.79, EG 596.8 vs 874.4.

minor.issue: At the same price, Analyze (live inputs) and the board sheet (stored inputs) differ a lot for some stocks: JPM 847.48 vs 1659.92, BAC 196.78 vs 398.82, TSLA 144.05 vs 137.15. The stored inputs are probably also being overwritten by the other writer, or are older.

Cash-flow methods don't make sense for banks: JPM DCF-20 -1767.34 and DFCF-Terminal 3920.54. The result is JPM +149.8% marked available with normal confidence, so intrinsic_value is set and it feeds buy levels. Consider skipping OCF/FCF methods for Financials, or always marking them low confidence.

A 10-year mean P/S for recent IPOs or companies that had no revenue explodes: RIVN Mean PS 1527 at price 11.67, LCID Mean PS 2033 at price 3.41. Consider a median, or capping or excluding pre-revenue years.
Negative average is formatted '$-356.67'. It should be '−$356.67', the same as the UI's usd().

ui_bugs.issue: Chip premium (e.g. AAPL +96%, CCI -5%) disagrees with the sheet's OptiIQ value (AAPL $241.80 / -29.7%; CCI is low-confidence in Analyze). This comes from the backend's second writer.
Rounding mismatch: the footer shows 'Growth ... 8.6% (6–10)' but the DCF note says '8.7% for 6-10' for MSFT. The footer uses round(g2,4) then toFixed(1); the note formats the unrounded value.

issues: Chip shows premium (price ÷ value − 1, +96%) while the sheet tag shows upside (value ÷ price − 1, −29.7%). The opposite sign conventions side by side are confusing. Consider labelling the chip '% over value' or using the same metric.

action_items: CRITICAL: stop the second writer on the shared Atlas valuation_board collection. Find which deployment (web app, or a production/older mobile backend) runs a board price/fundamentals loop with model_v=8 and a different formula, and turn it off or bring it in line. Or give the mobile board its own collection (e.g. valuation_board_mobile) or a unique model tag (e.g. MODEL_V='m8-nine') so neither side reads the other's docs.
Optional hardening: have GET /valuation/board recompute v/d/b from stored inputs (or keep a separate field written only by this backend) so the list and /valuation/board/{t} always agree.
Consider low confidence or skipping OCF/FCF methods for Financials (JPM +150% is shown as a normal-confidence value), and capping the mean P/S outliers for recent IPOs (RIVN, LCID).
Minor: format negative averages in the optiiq reason as −$X. Make the footer growth rounding match the method notes.
critical_code_review_comments: valuation_board.py: the price_loop and fundamentals_loop $set docs but never $unset old fields (capex_history from model 7 is left behind). Docs are keyed only by _id plus model_v, so any other writer using the same version number is accepted as valid.
valuation_board.py:413: the board list trusts the stored 'value', while /valuation/board/{t} recomputes from inputs. That is two sources of truth.
optiiq.py: when avg > 10x price the reason says 'Company data looks inconsistent' (RIVN), which hides the real cause (Mean PS outlier).

success_rate.backend: 83% (25/30; all 5 failures are the board v vs per-stock mismatch from the external writer)
success_rate.frontend: 95% (all flows work; the chip/sheet mismatch comes from the backend data)

rca_of_issue: Repro: GET /api/valuation/board -> AAPL v=175.06. GET /api/valuation/board/AAPL -> optiiq.value=241.80 at the same price 343.83. In Mongo, evaluate(doc) on the stored inputs gives 241.80. Right after our backend restarted, its price_loop (60s delay) wrote 241.80. A few minutes later the doc was back to 175.06 with a fresh price_ts, which this backend did not write. So another process writes the same collection with model_v 8 and a different model. Fix: isolate the collection or model tag, or switch off the other writer.
